samples.summary: `memoryFormat` short-circuit bypasses the `isFormat` validation that guards every other read path
samples.evidence: `getDateFormat()` returns `memoryFormat` at line 48 before the `isFormat()` check at line 51, and `setDateFormat(format)` (line 63) never validates its argument. The only caller, settings/page.tsx:71, does `setDateFormat(value as DateDisplayFormat)` — an unchecked cast of a raw Radix string. If any value other than "relative"/"exact" ever reaches that call (or a future caller), a failed write stores it in the mirror and `getDateFormat()` hands it straight back unvalidated, while the same junk coming from localStorage would be rejected. The guard is asymmetric: validate on read from storage, no validation at all on the in-memory path.

samples.summary: After one failed write, the tab is permanently frozen to the mirror and ignores all later storage/cross-tab changes
samples.evidence: `memoryFormat` is only ever cleared by a *successful* `localStorage.setItem` (line 66). Once a single write fails (transient quota, temporarily blocked storage), `getDateFormat()` returns the mirror forever for that session. The `storage` listener in `subscribe()` still fires on another tab's change, but `useSyncExternalStore` sees an unchanged snapshot, so the list never picks up the new preference — and if storage later becomes healthy nothing re-syncs until the user re-selects a value that happens to write successfully. The comment at lines 43-47 asserts "storage is known to be stale", which is only true immediately after the failure, not for the rest of the session.

samples.summary: `readStoredTheme` result is cast to `Theme` without validation; a junk stored value can throw from `classList.add`
samples.evidence: Line 65: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;`. The new helper hardens the *access* but still returns any string unvalidated. A stored value containing whitespace (e.g. left by an older build, an extension, or a manual edit) flows into the effect at line 87 as `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws `InvalidCharacterError` for a string with a space — an exception thrown from the provider's effect, i.e. the whole app. Any other junk value also silently mislabels `resolvedTheme` via the `theme as ResolvedTheme` cast at line 86. The sibling module added in this same change (`date-format-preference.ts`, `isFormat`) validates; this one does not.

samples.summary: Unguarded `formatDistanceToNow(new Date(...))` — the exact crash the diff's `parseDate` guard exists to prevent, bypassed at this call site
samples.evidence: `const formatted = formatDistanceToNow(new Date(createdAt), {...})` with no null/NaN check. Per the diff's own comment (document-list-utils.ts:84-87) `formatDistanceToNow` throws a RangeError on an invalid Date, and here that throw happens inside a table cell render, blanking the whole datasources table. This call site does not go through `parseDate`/`NO_DATE` at all. Pre-existing rather than introduced, but it is a live bypass of the guard this change formalizes.

`title={formatFullDateTime(value)}` returns `NO_DATE` ("—") when the value is missing or unparseable, so the cell shows an em dash whose hover tooltip is also an em dash. Omitting the attribute when there is no date would be more correct.

samples.summary: Every date cell mounts its own `useSyncExternalStore` subscription — two window listener pairs per row
samples.evidence: `DateCell` calls `useDateFormat()`, and `dateColumn` is used for both the Modified and Created columns (lines 875-876), so a list of N rows registers 2N `wafflebase-date-format-change` + 2N `storage` listeners on `window`. They are correctly removed on unmount, so this is not a leak, but every unrelated `storage` write (theme, board grid, slides widths) wakes all of them. A single subscription hoisted to the table would be equivalent and cheaper.

finding.summary: `readStoredTheme` result is cast to `Theme` without validation; a junk stored value can throw from `classList.add`
finding.evidence: Line 65: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;`. The new helper hardens the *access* but still returns any string unvalidated. A stored value containing whitespace (e.g. left by an older build, an extension, or a manual edit) flows into the effect at line 87 as `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws `InvalidCharacterError` for a string with a space — an exception thrown from the provider's effect, i.e. the whole app. Any other junk value also silently mislabels `resolvedTheme` via the `theme as ResolvedTheme` cast at line 86. The sibling module added in this same change (`date-format-preference.ts`, `isFormat`) validates; this one does not.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. theme-provider.tsx:25-31 `readStoredTheme` guards only the localStorage *access* (try/catch), returning `string | null` unvalidated; line 65 casts it with `as Theme`, where `|| defaultTheme` filters only null/empty string. Any other stored string becomes the `theme` state and reaches the effect's else-branch: line 86 `newResolvedTheme = theme as ResolvedTheme` (silently mislabels resolvedTheme, which is published through context and consumed for rendering) and line 87 `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws InvalidCharacterError for a token containing ASCII whitespace — an uncaught throw from the effect of the provider that wraps every route (docs/design/frontend.md:69). No validating guard exists on this path anywhere: the only in-app writer is writeStoredTheme (lines 33-40), and the URL-param (line 64) and postMessage (line 118) paths both validate against "light"|"dark", leaving the stored-value read as the sole unvalidated entry point, so `already-guarded` does not apply. The sibling module in the same change does validate (date-format-preference.ts:26-28 `isFormat`, :51), and docs/design/frontend.md:566-568,582-584 state the fallback-on-unrecognized-value contract while claiming ThemeProvider applies "the same two guards" — it applies the access guards but omits value validation, confirming the asymmetry. The precondition (junk value in localStorage from an older build, extension, or manual edit) is plausible rather than demonstrated, but that affects likelihood, not whether the described code exists; a crash path out of a top-level provider effect plus a broken resolvedTheme invariant is in-lane and blocking under the Correctness rubric.
